Daily Brief

The fallout from Tuesday's US midterm elections dominated global headlines Friday, with Democrats securing control of both chambers of Congress in what multiple outlets describe as a historic rebuke of the Trump administration [BBC, France 24, Nikkei Asia]. Tech stocks suffered a trillion-dollar sell-off as markets reacted to anticipated policy shifts, particularly around data center construction [France 24, Nikkei Asia]. The political earthquake has raised questions about Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's future, with the White House forced to deny imminent departures amid blame over the Iran war [BBC, France 24]. In South Africa, the ANC faces its worst electoral result since 1994, falling below 32% in local elections as voters punished the party over failing infrastructure [The Guardian]. Across Europe, a coordinated wave of hoax bomb threats disrupted flights and prompted evacuations at Irish media outlets, with a Russian extremist group denying involvement despite being named in threatening emails [BBC, Le Monde, Financial Times]. Meanwhile, the UN refugee agency warned ahead of COP31 that three-quarters of the world's displaced people now live on the frontlines of the climate crisis [RFI].

02 Geopolitics

ANC Suffers Worst Result Since End of Apartheid in South African Local Elections

  • The African National Congress received approximately 31.8% of the national vote with over 80% of ballots counted, down nearly 14 percentage points from 2021
  • The party is projected to lose its status as largest party in Gauteng and KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa's two most populous provinces
  • Voter turnout increased to 54.5%, up from 46% in 2021, amid widespread anger over water outages, power cuts, and infrastructure failures
  • Coalition negotiations are underway with final results expected Sunday; the Democratic Alliance received 24.1% and Jacob Zuma's MK party 9.3%

Kenyan Doomsday Cult Leader Sentenced to 200 Years for Murder of 191 People

  • Paul Mackenzie and 28 accomplices were sentenced for instructing cult members to starve their children to death to 'meet Jesus'
  • Mackenzie received 100 years for homicide and 100 years for starvation-related offenses, to run consecutively
  • Of the 191 victims, 190 were children; over 400 bodies were discovered in shallow graves in Shakahola forest in 2023
  • Prosecutors had sought the death penalty; the judge declined but called the sentence necessary to send 'an unmistakable message'
